tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

content.content:
# @entirehq mention watcher

Someone replies to `@entirehq` on X. You find out four hours later, because
nobody had that search tab open.

This closes that gap. A daemon polls the live `@entirehq` search every five
minutes, triages every new mention, and posts it to Slack in one of two
shapes so the ones worth acting on do not read like the rest.

```
★ `REPLY` @HaimantikaM · 17k followers
> Great points! We are also building something for this, would
> love to give you early access.
View on X · not a follower, offers early access · Oct 14 at 11:57 AM

`REPLY` @devsdv_ · @haatifff @neatlogs @EntireHQ Thanks 👍 · open · 172 followers
```

Priority gets a card and a `★` in the notification text; routine collapses to
one line. Every line leads with its kind in the same slot (`TWEET`, `REPLY`,
`QUOTE`), so the left edge answers "reply or tweet?" without reading the line.
On a live sample of 20 mentions this put 1 in priority and 16 in routine, with
3 muted.

It runs as a launchd agent — at login, across reboots, restarted if it dies,
independent of whether Claude Code is open. Zero tokens: a plain Node process
posting to a webhook, not an agent.

## Setup

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env       # fill in the five values below

recent-search endpoint needs a paid tier (~$200/mo). Two cookies cost nothing
and last months; when they expire the watcher says so in Slack rather than
returning nothing, which would read as "nobody is mentioning us."

```

   scrape ──→ parse ──→ filter ──→ diff ──→ post to Slack

                 (DOM        label

   ↓

  session-scoped watcher only when no agent is installed for this project. With
  the agent installed they stand down, so notifications never double up.
- **Slack is the only channel.** Nothing prints to your terminal; diagnostics
  go to `.claude/entirehq-watcher/watch.log` — including when Slack is the
  thing that's broken.
- **Two signals decide the tier, and they answer different questions.** A
  deterministic score measures reach (follower count, whether the author
  already follows `@entirehq`, verified, question, quote vs deep reply,
  switching intent). Claude Haiku reads the text and judges intent. A verdict
  wins whenever the classifier ran: reach does not make an emoji reply worth
  answering. The score decides alone when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unset or the
  call fails, so an outage degrades the ranking instead of dropping the post.
- **Engagement counts are deliberately unused.** A mention is seen within one
  poll of being posted, when every tweet still reads 0 likes and ~20 views, so
  traction cannot rank anything at the moment the decision has to be made.
  Author reach is known immediately; traction is not.
- **`IGNORE` demotes, it never drops.** A classifier false negative on a real
  support question would be invisible, and silence is the failure this tool
  exists to prevent. Only `X_MUTE_HANDLES` suppresses outright.
- **It reads X's JSON, not the page.** Playwright intercepts the
  `SearchTimeline` response instead of scraping `data-testid` attributes X
  rotates at will. Reply/quote classification uses real fields

  the 30-minute backoff cap, and three consecutive empty polls each fire

  re-alarm.

  full. Shorter `X_WATCH_POLL_MS` reduces the risk at the cost of more sessions.

  account, `X_MUTE_HANDLES` drops named accounts entirely, and
  `X_TEAM_HANDLES` pins teammates to the routine tier (their replies are a
  receipt, not a call to action).

  sees the plist names a different project and falls back to its hooks.
- **Automated browsing is contrary to X's ToS** — accepted knowingly, for one
  account's own brand mentions at low volume.

=== create ===
entire trail create — Create a trail for the current, a new, or no branch
Create a trail for the current, a new, or no branch.

With --repo, the trail is created on that repository through the API alone:
the local clone is not read or changed, nothing is pushed, and nothing is
prompted. --title, --base and --branch (or --no-branch) are then required, and
the branch must already exist on that repository.

Current repo: gh/elizabethsiegle/entirehq-mention-watcher  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
      --add-assignee strings   Assign user(s) by login
      --base string            Base branch (defaults to detected default branch)
      --body string            Trail body
      --branch string          Branch for the trail (defaults to current branch)
      --checkout               Check out the branch after creating it
      --no-branch              Create a branchless trail
      --priority string        Priority (urgent, high, medium, low, none)
      --status string          Initial status (defaults to open)
      --title string           Trail title
      --type string            Type (bug, feature, task)

      --repo string    Target repository as forge/owner/repo (e.g. gh/acme/app) or a clone URL; defaults to the origin remote

Current repo: gh/elizabethsiegle/entirehq-mention-watcher  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

entire trail show — Show a trail
Show a trail.

If <trail> is omitted, shows the trail for the current branch (or --branch).
Otherwise, <trail> may be a trail number, id, or branch in the target repo.

=== checkout ===
entire trail checkout — Check out a trail's branch
Check out the branch of a trail.

The trail may be given as the first argument or via --trail, as a number, id, or
branch. Without one, the trail for the current branch is used. The trail's branch
is checked out, fetching it from origin first when it only exists there.

With --worktree, the branch is checked out into a git worktree under
.entire/worktrees at the repo root instead of switching this checkout, and the
command prints a cd command for the new worktree. Gitignored files matching
.worktreeinclude patterns are copied into the worktree. When stdout is not a
terminal, only the worktree path is printed, so scripts can use
cd "$(entire trail checkout <trail> --worktree)".

This must be run from within a clone of the repository the trail belongs to; the
trail is looked up against that repository's origin remote.

input.command:
entire trail create \
  --branch feat/watch-entire-io-links \
  --checkout \
  --type feature \
  --priority medium \
  --title "Watch X for entire.io links as well as @entirehq" \
  --body "## Why

The watcher only sees tweets that tag \`@entirehq\`. Someone who posts a link to entire.io without tagging the account is invisible to it, and that is exactly the kind of organic share the team wants to see.

## What changes

- The live search becomes one combined query: the handle OR the domain. Still one Browserbase session per poll, so no added cost.
- X replaces links with t.co in \`full_text\`, so a domain match cannot be read off the text. The parser now carries the expanded URLs from \`entities.urls\` (and the anchor text on the DOM fallback path).
- Each tweet records how it matched: handle, link, or both.
- Slack and the Haiku triage prompt both use the match. A link-only share must not read as \"replied to @entirehq\".

## Validation

\`npm test\`, plus \`npm run preview\` against the live search." 2>&1

Trail is open and the work is sitting on its branch, tests green. Here's the scorecard.

**Trail 4** — "Watch X for entire.io links as well as @entirehq": https://entire.io/gh/elizabethsiegle/entirehq-mention-watcher/trails/4
Branch `feat/watch-entire-io-links`, based on local `main` (it has the two unpushed triage commits the feature builds on) with `origin/main` merged in for the trail runner configs. That merge is the only commit on the branch so far.

**What changed** (18 files, uncommitted in the working tree)
- One combined live search, `(@entirehq OR "entire.io")`, built from `X_OWN_HANDLE` + new `X_BRAND_DOMAIN`. Still one Browserbase session per poll, so no added cost.
- X rewrites every link in `full_text` to t.co, so the domain is unmatchable from tweet text. The parser now carries `entities.urls` (and the anchor display text on the DOM fallback path), and `filter.mjs` records `matchedVia`: handle, link, or both.
- Slack and the Haiku prompt both read it. A link-only share renders `TWEET · @somedev linked entire.io`, not `replied to @entirehq`, and the classifier is told the author is not waiting on a reply.

**The one that would have bitten you:** your live `.env` pinned `X_SEARCH_QUERY=@entirehq`, which overrides the new default, so this would have shipped as a no-op. I blanked that line and added `X_BRAND_DOMAIN=entire.io` (backup: `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/env.bak`). The running launchd daemon still holds the old code and old config in memory; it needs `npm run install-agent` to pick either up.

**Validation**
- `npm test`: 149 passing, 0 failing (was 124).
- Three live scrapes, nothing posted. Domain-only query: 20 results, all 20 correctly attributed `via link`, including replies like `@tokifyi Looks good. There's also this one: t.co/…` that never tag the account, which is exactly the blind spot. Combined query: 20 scraped, 19 after the own-post filter, 1 link match, and an @entirehq post linking the site was correctly dropped.
- `npm run preview`: 19 live mentions triaged end to end, one `via=both`.

**Known tradeoff, now in the README:** both terms share X's single ~20-result page, so a tag-chain burst can crowd out a link share in the same window. The Oct 17 check came back 20 of 20 full, 19 of them one reply chain.

**Needs your call:** I have not committed or pushed any of the code, so the trail has no work attached yet. Say the word and I'll commit to `feat/watch-entire-io-links` and push. Also worth knowing: `entire trail create` failed its first branch push with a bare `[remote rejected] (failed)`; a plain `git push` of the same branch went through on the first try, so it looks transient rather than a permissions wall.

input.command:
entire trail create \
  --branch feat/collapse-reply-chains \
  --base feat/watch-entire-io-links \
  --checkout \
  --type feature \
  --priority medium \
  --title "Collapse long reply chains instead of posting every link in them" \
  --body "## Why

One tag chain can fill the channel on its own. A live check on 2026-10-17 came back with 20 mentions, 19 of which were replies inside two threads: one account thanking twelve people one reply at a time, and a restaurant thread where @entirehq was incidental. Every one of them posted its own Slack line. Nineteen lines that say nothing is how a channel gets muted, and a muted channel is the failure this tool exists to prevent.

## What changes

A routine mention is allowed a budget of individual posts per thread per window. Past the budget the rest of that thread collapses into one line (\"7 more replies in this thread\"), one line per poll at most.

- Threads are identified by X's \`conversation_id_str\`. The DOM fallback path does not expose it, so it groups by author there, which is the same flood in practice.
- Priority never collapses. The budget applies to the routine tier only: silence on something actionable is the one outcome worth more than a tidy channel.
- The budget persists across polls, so a thread that drips in over an hour cannot restart it every five minutes.
- A collapsed batch is marked seen only once Slack accepts its summary line, matching the existing per-tweet rule.

## Validation

\`npm test\`, plus \`npm run preview\` against the live search, which currently contains exactly the chains that motivated this." 2>&1 | tail -6
